transcript: Went to the Saturday farmers market at the Ferry Building. Bought peaches, sourdough, and these giant purple carrots. Ran into my old roommate Leo. Then spent the afternoon making a peach galette with my mom over FaceTime. It came out ugly but really good. Ate it on the balcony at golden hour.

spec.moment: Eating the homemade peach galette on the balcony during golden hour.

elements.name: peach galette
elements.look: A rustic, uneven golden-brown galette filled with warm baked peach slices.

elements.name: purple carrots
elements.look: A bundle of oversized deep purple carrots tied with twine in a paper market tote.

elements.name: sourdough loaf
elements.look: A crusty round sourdough boule dusted with flour.

elements.name: balcony railing
elements.look: A warm iron balcony railing lined with small potted herbs.

elements.name: smartphone on a stand
elements.look: A small phone propped on the table, its screen glowing with warm golden light.

spec.scene: A wooden balcony floor is bathed in warm honey-toned light. In the center, a rustic outdoor bistro table holds a warm, imperfect peach galette on a ceramic plate, slightly larger than life. Beside it sits a small propped smartphone glowing with gentle light. To the left rests a paper tote filled with large deep-purple carrots and a round sourdough loaf. A black wrought-iron railing with tiny potted basil plants lines the back edge, catching the long golden rays of late sun.
spec.title: Golden Hour Galette
spec.caption: It turned out ugly, but eating it on the balcony was perfect.
